In the as-extruded condition (Fig. 2a), the major peak is observed at 42, and the corresponding crystal structure of austenite can be determined as B2 with a lattice parameter of a = 0.3102 nm.
The crystal structure of the martensite ( Fig. 2b) is B19 0 with lattice parameters of a = 0.3069 nm, b = 0.4105 nm, c = 0.4888 nm and b = 103.2.
The as-extruded and 400 C–3 h aged specimens consist of a single B2 austenite phase without any detectable precipitates.
The B19 0 martensite phase was observed between the precipitates.

In contrast, spindle-shaped precipitates were clearly observed in the 550 C–3 h and 650 C–3 h aged specimens. Fig. 3 a shows the bright-field image of the 550 C–3 h sample, where the inset is the magnified image of area B.

Fig. 3 c shows the bright-field image of the 650 C–3 h specimen. It is clear that the precipitates are quite large compared with the 550 C–3 h specimen, with a length that varies from 80 nm to 300 nm and a width of 50 nm.
According to the SAD pattern, the fine striations, which can be seen inside the martensite phase, were determined as (0 0 1)B190 compound twins.

The (0 0 1)B190 compound twins were also observed in the 650 C–3 h specimen, which can be confirmed by the SAD pattern shown in Fig. 3 d (taken from area D in Fig. 3 c), indicating that the main twinning mode observed in the martensite phase was not affected by the aging temperature.
The NiTiHfPd polycrystalline alloy undergoes a B2 (cubic) to B19 0 (monoclinic) phase transformation under zero stress.

It was revealed that precipitation hardening significantly improved the shape memory properties of the NiTiHfPd alloy.
Shape memory alloys (SMA) have the unique ability to recover large deformations upon heating or by removal of load owing to their capability to undergo thermoelastic martensitic transformations [1].

The initial drop in TT with aging at 400 C is attributed to the formation of precipitates with very small size and very short interparticle distance. Thus, the resistance for martensite nucleation increases, and formation of martensite requires more energy change, which in turn requires further undercooling in the course of the forward transformation [34].

In contrast, the increase in the thermal hysteresis with stress of the 650 /C176C–3 h aged sample can be linked to a relatively weaker matrix that results in easier dislocation generation with stress.
